items.title: NEW — `View::autofocus()` (A45) focuses in a MICROTASK, before the frame's rendering step, so an input inside a subtree that becomes focusable only during rendering (kolt's overlay panel is `visibility: hidden` until a ResizeObserver callback places it and flips it visible, overlay.vl:443/:554) is not focusable when `focus()` runs and the call is a no-op — the browser rule, not a race: `focus()` needs a connected, rendered, visible, non-inert target AT THE CALL; "just created" is never the problem, "still hidden" is
items.discussion: the owner's find (2026-09-07): `element.focus()` fires and the browser "doesn't take it"; the old `set_timeout(1)` only happened to land after the ResizeObserver flip; std's doc claims the microtask is enough, which is true only for a subtree that is visible at build time
items.body: Two halves. (1) `autofocus` (and `on_mount`'s doc) state the precondition, and `autofocus` becomes bounded and frame-aware without a millisecond: attempt in the microtask; if `document.activeElement` is not the element, attempt again in the next animation frame, and once more in the frame after (ResizeObserver and layout-driven flips land in the rendering step between); then stop, no timer, no arbitrary delay. (2) The formal shape for an overlay is that focus is a consequence of the SHOW: an `on_shown`-class hook the overlay driver runs when it flips visibility (or `<dialog>.showModal()`, whose focusing steps run once the dialog is rendered and which makes the rest of the document inert on its own — the platform's version of kolt's `inert` toggle), focusing the panel's `[autofocus]` descendant. Pin (1) with the ui_rows DOM stub extended by a `visibility` flag on `focus()` (a hidden element refuses), and document (2) on `Overlay`'s guide page. Note the one case no timing fixes: iOS Safari ignores programmatic `focus()` outside a user gesture.
